title: Replacement in an independent product law
statement: Let $V$ and $D$ be finite sets, let $\mu_v$ be a probability mass function on $D$ for each $v\in V$, and fix $v_0\in V$. First sample $a$ from $\mu_{v_0}$, then form the independent product law using $\mu_{v_0}$ replaced by the point mass at $a$. The resulting mixture of product laws equals the independent product law formed from the original family $(\mu_v)_{v\in V}$.
hypotheses_covered: $\mathrm{law}:V\to\mathrm{PMF}(D)$ is a family of probability mass functions
